subject: Granular term structure and retention-swap proposal for PulseAI
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <anna@pulse.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.o@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Granular term structure and retention-swap proposal for PulseAI

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the candid call yesterday. You asked us to put together a concrete number set showing how we’d match the incumbent economic while factoring in the one-time migration support they’re offering. I’ve attached a draft workbook (pulse-migration-costs.xlsx) and a short RFP response PDF.

High-level proposal for discussion:
- 12-month base term with a blended per-token parity to their current sticker (we can hold list pricing and push most incentive into a migration credit).
- A split migration credit: 60% upfront credit applied to invoices over first 3 months, 40% amortized as a monthly seat-credit over 9 months (reduces churn risk).
- 150 hours of dedicated migration engineering + 30 hours onboarding enablement (tagged as billable credit) — technical escrow for connectors to their legacy stack.
- Optional incremental 6 months of reduced egress pricing for archival flows (to match estimated backup costs).

Questions for your team: what portion of the incumbent’s value is actual spend vs. internal ops cost (e.g., dedicated SRE time)? That will affect how aggressive we need to be on credits versus list reductions.

Next steps: if Pulse likes the structure we’ll prepare a one-page term sheet and a contract amendment showing the amortized credit schedule. If you’d like, we can also run a short benchmark with a 2-week pilot to validate latency/throughput at your current seq-lens — that helps reduce migration risk and justify lower credits.

Thanks — I’ll await your feedback.

—Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Anna Park <anna@pulse.ai>

Subject: Re: Granular term structure and retention-swap proposal for PulseAI

Priyom —

Appreciate the thoroughness. A few clarifications from our side after a quick read:

1) The incumbent currently shows ~$270k/quarter in billings to our finance team. Operationally we estimate ~120 SRE hours/month tied to tuning/ops across the stack (we’d consider that part of the incumbent value).
2) The migration support being offered by them is a 180-hour package plus a 1-month reduced egress credit on backup flows.
3) We care about two things in priority order: zero-regression on latency at P95 for our 1k-3k token tails, and a clean migration window that doesn’t disrupt our daily rate limit behavior.

On credits: our CFO is willing to consider an amortized credit, but it needs to be explicit how it shows against our ARR and the timing of invoice impacts (we’ll need that to model churn/forecast).

Can you also include a short note on how Redwood will handle model parity failures (if inference quality regresses vs incumbent) and what rollback/fallback operational steps you’ll commit to?

If you can send a revised one-pager and a quick sketch of the pilot plan, we’ll loop in procurement to move toward a term sheet.

Best,
Anna
VP Product, PulseAI

Subject: Fwd: PulseAI questions — proposed concession structure and pilot

Team —

Pulse pushed back on the absolute $ credit (they want amortization clarity for ARR modeling) and wants an explicit quality/fallback commitment. Below is my recommended response and trade-offs for us to sign off internally before sending to Pulse:

Recommended concession (keeps economics contained, reduces churn risk):
- Migration credit: $120k total applied as follows: $72k (60%) applied as invoice credits across first 3 billing cycles; $48k (40%) issued as a monthly seat-credit of $5.333k over 9 months. Notes: seat-credit shows as contra-revenue to our invoices; the upfront portion reduces cash collected but is straightforward for procurement.
- Support: 160 dedicated migration hours (we absorb 20 hours beyond incumbent package) + 40 enablement hours. Any additional engineering time billed at T&M (pre-agreed rate).
- Quality guardrails: run a 2-week pilot against a 1M token test-set that mirrors their 1k-3k tail distribution. If P95 latency/regression exceeds agreed thresholds or quality delta > 2.5% on key metrics, we trigger an automatic rollback to incumbent routing for affected endpoints for up to 30 days while we remediate (no charge for mitigation hours up to 40).
- Egress: match 1 month of reduced egress pricing; additional months can be scoped as add-on at discounted band.

Trade-offs to consider:
- Upfront cash hit vs. amortized exposure (we are effectively spreading $48k over 9 months of revenue recognition). If procurement insists on full-of-credit upfront, we should ask for either a 9-month minimum commitment or a shorter payment window.
- Pilot acceptance criteria must be crisp — I propose we define 4 measurements (P95 latency, avg token cost, model score delta on Pulse's eval set, and error rate on structured outputs).

Can Neha and Laura confirm we’re comfortable taking the $120k structure on a 12-month term and sign off on the rollback SLA language? Connor, please confirm the pilot scope and that 160 hours + 40 enablement is feasible operationally.

—Priyom

Subject: RE: Granular term structure and retention-swap proposal for PulseAI — term sheet + pilot sketch

Anna / procurement team —

Thanks for the clear priorities. Attached is a one-page term sheet and the pilot sketch in the Drive folder (link below). Key points summarized:

1) Financials: 12-month base term. Total incentive package $120,000 broken into $72,000 immediate invoice credits (applied across first 3 cycles) + $48,000 amortized as monthly contra credits over 9 months. We explicitly state how each line shows in invoices to help your finance model.
2) Migration & enablement: 160 hours migration engineering (Redwood covers 20 hours above incumbent): 40 hours onboarding enablement (recorded as credited hours). Additional time at pre-agreed T&M.
3) Quality & rollback: Pilot acceptance criteria (P95 latency threshold, model-score delta <= 2.5% on joint eval set, structured-output error rate threshold). If pilot fails acceptance we will: a) route impacted calls to incumbent variant for up to 30 days, b) provide up to 40 remediation hours free, c) jointly time-box fixes and re-run acceptance.
4) Egress: 1 month matched reduced egress band; subsequent months can be added as a paid add-on with 20% discount to list.

Pilot sketch (summary): 2-week run, 1M token test-set representative of production tails, 3 staged phases (baseline capture, staged traffic at 10/30/100% production, acceptance run). Connor will serve as primary technical PM for Redwood.

If this structure looks good I can convert the one-pager into a clean execution term sheet and route to legal for a simple amendment. If procurement needs a different amortization (e.g., all-upfront credit) we should request a 9-month minimum revenue commitment in exchange.
